utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Novakovic, I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given yesterday that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. If you are ready, Mr. Weber, then you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session. I take it that you want the whole Chamber to move into private session, not only the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honour. Further Cross-examination by Mr. Weber: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Novakovic.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday I showed you an image and asked if you recognised Mihajlo Lukic. Today I am now going to play a video-clip, and could you please watch this clip and the individuals depicted in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm now going to ask Mr. Laugel to play a clip from Exhibit P1592. The clip will commence playing at the 1:59 mark, and I've asked Mr. Laugel to pause the clip after approximately 11 seconds. The Prosecution is going to play the clip without any sound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The clip is now paused at the 2:10 mark. Mr. Novakovic, are you able to identify Mihajlo Lukic in this video?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looks like him. This one person looks like him, but I cannot say with any certainty that it's him. You know, it was how many years ago?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The one person that you believe to be him, what is that person wearing in the video?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's not on this still.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. Do you recall what he was wearing in the video?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the reason why I'm not sure, because I've never seen him in uniform. I'm not sure if that's the person in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please return to open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, before we do that, the witness says he's not on -- the person he thinks or looks like Mr. Lukic is not on this still. Now, what is the Chamber supposed to understand? Is there any portion where Mr. Lukic is seen so that we are able to follow the evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We do have a still from this portion that we showed yesterday I can call back up to the screen, if it's -- that would be D744, page 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I can ask if that's the individual that he believes again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps that would be good.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because I do not know why we stop here, where the supposed Mr. Lukic is not visible, rather than at any other spot where one could see him, for the witness also to describe any -- but if you say the still would do better, then that's okay as far as I'm concerned. Then I wonder what the video was good for, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just trying to give the opportunity to the witness to view the full images, and I understand your concern. Could we please have Exhibit D744, page 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, in the image that is before you, do you see the person that you believe to be Mihajlo Lukic from the video-clip that we just saw?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at this still, it could be Mihajlo Lukic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I'm not sure. I cannot be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the court usher please hand the witness a pen and could the witness please then circle the individual that he believes to be Mihajlo Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which he believes to be possibly --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mihajlo Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just so we have a clear record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time the Prosecution would tender the marked still image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number for D744 marked by the witness will be P3167, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3167 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, since it is identifying a member -- a former member of the operative, we would ask that it be provisionally under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Former members are -- I don't know. That is not within the ruling, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. I was being --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sources, BIA operatives, and locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please return to open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We return into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At transcript page 14074 of your testimony last fall, you indicated that you could not recall whether you received a salary increase between the 10th of July and the 10th of August, 1995. On that same page, you stated, in response to a question to whether you received a per diem in July or August 1995: "Well, I cannot tell you exactly. It was 17 years ago." Yesterday, at transcript page 19963, you stated in response to my question about a 20 per cent salary increase in October 1995 the following: "Look, in July and August 1995, I was also in the Krajina, and I believe my salary was then increased by 50 per cent." On the next page you stated: "From the 5th or 6th of July, I believe, until the 5th or 6th of August, 1995, that was the time I was in the Republic of Serbian Krajina." What is the reason that you now recall the exact amount of your salary increase, where you were assigned in July and August 1995, and the precise dates of your assignment?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you. You showed me a decision that I signed, increasing my salary by 50 per cent. The period when I was in the Republic Serbian Krajina is a period I now remember was exactly that. So my salary was increased for that period by 50 per cent, and I was separately rewarded by 20 per cent more in salary, although I was already back in Serbia, and I believe that that was a reward for the jobs that I had done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, just so it's clear: At the time that you made the comment, is it correct that I had just shown you a salary increase of 20 per cent in October 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the papers and the documents you showed me, I see that it was, and I believe if you got these documents from my personnel file, then they must be authentic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Last fall you testified about one occasion where you were in the Krajina between November and December 1994. Why do you now recall being assigned to the Krajina on a second occasion between July and August 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean why I didn't mention it then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have a page number, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir. Could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, are you asking me how come I did not mention then that I had been there also in July and August 1995 when I was speaking about November and December 1994?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you how you recall today that you were in the Krajina in July and August 1995. That's my -- the gist of my question. Could you tell us how you recall that today?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was here before, we discussed the time periods that you asked about, the time lines you asked about, and I answered those questions. I wasn't talking about July 1995 or 1996 or 1997. There are many things that I remember I did in 1996, for instance. When you put a question, I answer to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when I asked you whether you received a salary increase in July and August 1995 when you were last here, what is the reason that you did not recall being assigned to the Krajina at that time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same pages, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That would be page 14074 where I asked him about that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember. Maybe I overlooked it. It was such a long time ago, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please return to 65 ter 6545, page 3 of the B/C/S and page 5 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, could I just -- I do think that it would be more fair to the witness, if my learned friend is going to -- because I've just read the transcript, and it's hard to keep up, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please, Mr. Weber, if you put something to the witness what he said, then to read the question and answer, and if it's too much, the gist of it and with the precise page reference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, before you there's a decision dated July 13 of 1995 from a Milan Prodanic, the head of the 8th Administration. This decision indicates that you received a 50 per cent salary increase because you were deployed for the execution of official duties in Prizren from 10 July 1995 to 10 August 1995. Directing your attention to the lower left corner --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have the bottom of the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does your signature appear on this document?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the signature without a date. I signed that I received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 6545 into evidence and requests that this exhibit be placed under seal. The Prosecution is tendering the five excerpts that -- from his personnel file that have been discussed with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6545 will receive number P3168, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Let me just check, Mr. Weber. Any need to have it under seal? Yes, under seal. Admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified at transcript page 14017 that you were in Visegrad on the 1st or 2nd of June, 1995. I'd like to ask you whether or not you saw any Red Berets in Visegrad at this time.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember on what occasion I went to Visegrad what the incident was. Could you tell me more about my testimony then?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 14017, Mr. Jordash asked you: "When did you attend Visegrad?" Your answer was: "It could have been either the 1st or 2nd of June as far as I can remember. I -- I mean, I believe it was the 2nd of June. I really can't remember the exact date after such a long time. "Q. Fair enough and -- Then His Honour said: "And we are talking about the hostage crisis. Who are the hostages?" Sir, I believe this was in relation to your --

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- if that refreshes your recollection. During this occasion, did you see any Red Berets in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object, and I would appreciate it if my learned friend would be more precise when he says Red Berets. Because this is a highly sensitive issue in this case, would he please tell the witness which unit precisely he means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- this is comment on the question. If the witness -- this is inappropriate, Mr. Petrovic. You should refrain from making observations which could even be understood as messages. The witness may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then in Visegrad I didn't see any Red Berets. I believe I stated in my testimony at an earlier trial that I was met by a representative of the State Security Department of Republika Srpska and somebody from the VRS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At transcript page 14036 of your earlier testimony, you were asked the following question: "Following the massacres in Srebrenica, was there any issue which arose as a result of Muslims fleeing those events?" Your answer was: "In the area of the Uzice centre in that period, there was a large influx from the area of Zepa to the area of the Uzice centre. I cannot recall the exact time-frame. I think it could be August." Is it correct --

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that this -- that you understood this question and answer related to events which occurred in July and August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It was July/August 1995. I don't know the exact time period, but I know that after those activities in Zepa a large number of civilians fled to the territory of Uzice, and they were put up in Branicko Polje, at least a part of them. There was a collection centre established there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know about the events that occurred in Srebrenica and Zepa?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, the events in Srebrenica and Zepa, even now, looking back, they probably coincide with my stint in Krajina. So when I got there, I was briefly -- I was mainly briefed and got my information from -- from the media reports and from the -- what was available in the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 6547.1. The Prosecution requests that this document not be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I meanwhile ask one additional question. You told us about increase of salary between the 10th of July and 10th of August, that you didn't remember, it's too long ago. That's what you said in -- in the fall of last year.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You didn't remember that you were in the Krajina in July and early August in 1995, in the Krajina, and that was the reason why you got extra salary? You don't remember that? You didn't remember that at -- in -- when was it? October. You'd forgotten about your presence in the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, looking at the decision, I believe that is it. That is for that stay there. It's an increase of salary as remuneration for that trip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But did you not remember then where you were in July/early August when you answered these questions? "When I was on field missions, I received per diem," you said. Do you remember to be -- didn't you remember in October of last year that you had been in the Krajina in July and August 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if anyone ever asked me, actually, where I was at the time. If it's in the transcript, I should like to see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was asked to you is: "Did you receive any increase in your salary between the 10th of July and the 10th of August, 1995?" And then you said: "An increase in salary? I can't remember now. It's too long ago. When I was on field missions, I received per diems." This seems to be a lack of recollection of what happened or an increase of salary in July and August 1995, and you told us now that you were in the Krajina at that time. My question is: Didn't you remember that when you testified last October?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember a decision was shown to me, but I can't say with any certainty. I knew in October that I had been in Krajina at that time, but I can't remember the exact question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll carefully look at the transcript of your testimony at that time. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that you were in the Krajina during Operation Storm and you forgot that?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can now state that I was in Krajina in that period and that at the beginning of Operation Storm I returned to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, I'd like to turn your attention to the document that's before you. This is a Republic of Serbia State Security Department JATD Official Note dated 5 March 1996. I'd like to direct your attention to the bottom of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please have that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the author of this Official Note, Milan Maksimovic?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know Mr. Maksimovic?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that in that period of time he was within the unit. Now, what was his specific task? Was he within the unit? Was he on the reserve? I mean, I'm talking about that particular period that we are discussing now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to discuss with you an earlier period that's referred to in this Official Note.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please go back up to the top portion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first sentence of this Official Note states: "In the period between 18 June and 25 June, 1995, I went to Srebrenica on a number of occasions with the knowledge of the Service." Were you aware or ever become aware of any members of the JATD or other members of the Serbian DB who went to Srebrenica in late June 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. That was not within my purview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Official Note continues to state: "In the mentioned period, I met Milan Lukic from Visegrad in the hotel in Bratunac. He was dressed in a NATO uniform and wore a red beret with no insignia. At that time there were about five to six soldiers from Visegrad with Lukic who were similarly dressed, wearing the red beret as a part of their uniform. I met that same group, equipped the same, ten to 15 days later in the operations of the liberation of Zepa. When I met them in Bratunac and Srebrenica, the following were in the company of this group." There is a name stated, "a CRDB Bajina Basta operative, Boskovic Borko, a member of our reserve composition. When I met them near Zepa, I was in the company of," the name of the same individual mentioned in the previous paragraph, "an SDB Uzice operative. In the same period, following the liberation of Srebrenica, the following showed up wearing our uniform with our insignia: Radivojevic, Milutin, and Nakarada, Svetozar -- "

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you are apparently reading from a translation which is not exactly the same as we have on our screen. Is there any reason why you take a different version of the translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. I was working off the translation that I had been provided. I do see that this is slightly -- I see that there are some differences in the translation. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I do not know what questions you'll put to the witness and to what extent the slight differences may play a role there. Please keep that in mind when you ask questions. And if need be, read again from the translation we have in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and thank you for bringing that to my attention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is correct that members of the JATD wore Red Berets and green camouflage uniforms similar to those worn by NATO forces?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, that's the kind of uniforms they wore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if any hotels in Bratunac were used by commanders of the VRS, including Ratko Mladic?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I absolutely have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Milutin Radivojevic, Svetozar Nakarada, or Borko Boskovic or ever become aware of these people as members of the JATD?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the end of the answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, these names mean nothing to me except for Maksimovic and Mihajlo Lukic. And Milan Lukic up there, yes, I heard of him. As for the rest, I know nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can we --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we have a redaction of the reference to Mihajlo Lukic at page 15, line -- he is a former -- I've been treating it cautiously, not knowing whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't it true that yesterday a lot of questions were put, I think even in open session?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Former operatives are not within the scope of the ruling.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And similarly, one document which was admitted under seal was dealt with yesterday at length in open session. So let's try to clearly stick to what the ruling was, that is, IBA [sic] sources -- BIA sources, BIA operatives. That means those who are now BIA operatives, still BIA operatives, and BIA locations. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Official Note indicates that there were encounters between a member of the Uzice CRDB and members of the JATD with Milan Lukic in Bratunac, Srebrenica, and Zepa at different times in late June and early -- and, I'm sorry, July 1995. Did you know or ever become aware of these meetings?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. I see from this note, the date, that this is when I was in the Krajina. I mean, this is the month of June, and I was there. This is just before that. I absolutely have no knowledge of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mihajlo Lukic ever discuss these events with you?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain how it is possible that Mihajlo Lukic never mentioned these events to you? Yesterday, you stated that the two of you discussed the Lukic cousins. Did you not discuss anything about them in more detail?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I know Mihajlo Lukic very, very well and we are good friends. Mihajlo Lukic and Milan Lukic are two different persons. I mean, the families of Mihajlo Lukic and Milan Lukic are completely different too. Now, why? They are very distantly related. I mean, they have the same distant ancestors. I don't know to what extent I can explain this to you. When Milan Lukic was in the area, in the houses of the Lukics, I mean, this Milan Lukic is not from that area at all. He was not even born there where Milan -- Mihajlo Lukic was born, his father, grandfather, whatever. But since Milan Lukic was in Visegrad, the uncle of Mihajlo Lukic was wounded in his house, and he even died. He succumbed to these wounds. I have to say that Mihajlo Lukic never looked upon the stay of Milan Lukic in that area favourably. These are two different families.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say he "never looked upon the stay of Milan Lukic in that area favourably," what area are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area of Visegrad. From the very beginning of these war operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecution's case is that the interactions between Milan Lukic and the members of the Serbian DB do not show that the accused were concerned about protecting Muslims but, in fact, had other contacts that were of quite a different nature with Milan Lukic is included. He's included training Milan Lukic and some of his men and also encountering Milan Lukic and being with him in July 1995. Would you care to provide any comments on our position based on the interactions or contacts between the Serbian DB and Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I just object, for the record. We haven't had notice that it was alleged that the accused were responsible for training Milan Lukic or his men either in the indictment, the pre-trial brief, or the opening statement. I think it was mentioned by Mr. Weber at some point during the Defence case, but that was the first time we understood that that was -- or we were provided with a scintilla of notice about that. And secondly, it would be useful even at this late stage to know precisely what it is is being alleged concerning the - and I put -- I use Mr. Weber's words - "encounters" that it is alleged that the accused are responsible for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd be happy to answer, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd be happy to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the information in the testimony that's been elicited through this witness was in the context of the Serbian DB taking actions to curb certain extremism, and that included actions taken against Milan Lukic. It is from this context that the Defence offers the actions taken by the Serbian DB against Milan Lukic. The Prosecution has brought forward information of other contacts that the DB had with Milan Lukic. We are just offering it to rebut the reason that the Defence has asserted as a defence to the accused's intent in relation to actions carried out by the Serbian DB to curb extremism.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, at this moment what has to be done is to give an opportunity to the witness to respond what the Prosecution thinks is contradicting the Prosecution's case, isn't it? And that is done using this document. Now, the battle on whether you have had sufficient notice at this moment, it's not primarily an issue of giving notice to the Defence, but at this moment it's to put it to the witness in order to give him an opportunity to comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, and I think that is right in relation to the so-called encounters. It's not right in relation to the training. This witness hasn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- said anything which would require Mr. Weber to put that allegation. He was doing it in order to indicate so that the Prosecution would plead, at a later date, that the accused trained Milan Lukic. It's to slip in a new allegation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If you could make them separate. And if you want to ask a question about training, then perhaps do not do it in a way by putting to the witness, but ask whether the witness is aware of any -- has any knowledge about training rather than encounters. Mr. Weber, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honours, I discussed the training with the witness last fall. I will just keep it focused on this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any comments on the interaction between the Serbian DB and Milan Lukic based on this document?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no comment. Especially I do not know what it was that Mihajlo Lukic could put on Milan Lukic. I really don't know about that in any way. I mean, they were not close. I can assume that this encounter may have taken place, but for Mihajlo Lukic to train Milan Lukic, I mean, what point of contact would they have?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I ask one question, Mr. Weber. When this document was shown to you and you responded to the dates described in the document, that is, late June 1995, by saying, "Well, I wasn't there. I was at the time in the Krajina." If my recollection serves me well, I think yesterday you said that you left for the Krajina the 5th or the 6th of July and then returned the 5th or the 6th of August. And I also remember that there was the 10th of July. But I did not understand from your testimony yesterday, neither from your testimony today, that you're in the Krajina between the 18th and the 25th of June. Could you assist me in understanding your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. Even now I made this comment stating that I was in the Krajina at a certain period, but I see now that it's June, June/July. I mean, I couldn't see from this, because I see this note was written in 1996, and it concerns information from 1995 and then the question is being put as to where I was in 1995. So that is how I confused the two. In this period I hadn't left for the Krajina yet. This was a week or ten days before I'd left. I mean, I roughly went, say, on the 3rd, 4th of July and returned on the 5th or 6th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Well, you say you were not aware of the date described, that it was -- because you said it was March 1996. Let me then read your answer: "Absolutely. I see from this note the date that this was written. I was in the Krajina. I mean, is the month of June, and I was there. This is just before that. I absolutely have no knowledge." So apparently when you answered that question, you were perfectly aware that the events described here were in June and that you were not mistaken by March 1996, because you specifically referred to June. So therefore your answer, where you said, "I mean, I couldn't see from this because I see this note was written in 1996 and it concerns information from 1995," "but I see now that it's June," but in your previous answer you refer to June as well as, so apparently you were aware that the events described were about June, whereas you left for the Krajina only in July. It puzzles me slightly. Please proceed, Mr. Weber. But I give you an opportunity to further explain if you wish to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean, I don't remember mentioning March at all, what you referred to just now. I really got confused by the dates here. I mean, I would like to say that in this period that the note pertains to, I see from it, I was in Uzice. In the beginning of July 1995, I went to the Krajina, and I returned in the beginning of August 1995. However, I saw the date up there that it was written in March 1996, and it has to do with information from 1995, so I did not understand that. I don't see for which purpose this note was written up. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to think that the information in this Official Note is not correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders 65 ter 6547.1 into evidence. It's just the single excerpt. We ask that it be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We object to the tendering of this document. Had we had notice of this document during the Prosecution case, we could have taken steps to investigate this material. We could have spoken to Mihajlo, for example. We could have conducted investigations into what was happening in this location at that time. We could have spoken to Mr. Novakovic during the proofing session. We would have had a reasonable opportunity to be able to deal with this material. We've been deprived of that opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber. Or Mr. Petrovic first.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we subscribe to what Mr. Jordash says. Also, we would like to add that on the basis of this document and on the basis of the questions put by my learned friend Mr. Weber, one may conclude that the Prosecution case is being extended in this way and they are trying to say directly or indirectly that this group that was with Milan Lukic is linked to the DB of Serbia. We haven't heard that until now. Until now this has not been the Prosecution case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, in terms of timing, the -- as Your Honours are aware, this document was the subject of the reason that the witness was recalled, and the information in it, the names in particular, were not available to the Prosecution until the 12th of March, 2012. So this is information that recently became available to us. We have sought the recall of the witness on this basis, and we've made submissions as to why we would like to recall him concerning this. As I've indicated today, the reason the Prosecution sought to recall the witness is because the Defence seeks to rely upon, as a defence, that actions were taken against Milan Lukic by the Serbian DB. This document is being offered to show that there were other contacts between the Serbian DB and Milan Lukic that did not involve any type of punitive actions or remedial actions taken against him. That's why we're offering it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you are talking about newly received materials. Was the Defence made aware of what you received recently so that they could have anticipated on -- on what would have triggered your request? Not only that it was new material, but also what that material was, was it disclosed?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We -- we -- this was the subject of the recall. We filed it as attached to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I see that, but I'm -- I'd just like to know whether once you received that you had immediately disclosed that to the Defence so that they would know on the basis of what material exactly you are -- you had received you sought to recall the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It was disclosed with the motion to recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Jordash, the material not being available in fall of last year, everything being disclosed to the Defence so that the Defence would be aware that this new material triggered the request for a recall, does that in any way influence your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's not irrelevant, but it's not the core point. The core point is that the Prosecution have known since the beginning of this case, since we've filed our -- at least since we've filed our Defence pre-trial brief, what our position was in relation to Lukic. They had ample notice that we were suggesting that the accused had been involved in making an arrest. They had ample notice that it was alleged by the Defence that we had nothing to do with Mr. Lukic other than the arrest. The Prosecution had ample opportunity to conduct reasonable investigations well in advance to give us the same opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber denies the objection. The document is admissible. Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6547.1 will receive number P3169, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3169 is admitted into evidence. Any need to have to under seal, Mr. -- and, please, on the basis of the ruling and not on overcautious.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Republic of Serbia, just out of fairness to them, has requested that with respect to the collection of unredacted materials to -- I would just like to -- if we could keep it provisionally under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We -- it's admitted provisionally under seal. In order to avoid whatever misunderstanding when I said the Chamber denies the objection, I perhaps should have said the Chamber denies the objections, because they were of a different nature. The one was about notice and the other one was about extending the Prosecution's case. So both objections are denied. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, I'd like to return to your previous testimony about the investigation into explosions at a gas station and a transformer station in Kremna during June 1991 and your comments provided on documents D427 and D432, marked for identification. At transcript page 13591, you stated: "Through our operative work, we managed to establish that the explosion at the gas station, as well as the explosion at the transformer station, which is about 2 or 3 kilometres away on Sargan mountain was carried out by the same people." In your comments on Exhibit D432, you stated: "The public security investigated and determined that the used explosive devices were of the same kind and that the time of the explosions match, which indicate the perpetrators were the same. The state security was involved in the further investigation into the perpetrators until they were arrested." At transcript page 13958, you stated that the culprits were determined to be Muslims who hailed from the territory of Visegrad. Is it correct that the Serbian DB further investigated this matter until it was determined that Bosnian Muslims from Visegrad committed these offences?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The further investigation was conducted both by the DB and the SUP of Uzice. That was before the beginning of war in Bosnia. So we addressed officially the authorities of Bosnia through our contacts, asking them to find in the records who owned that vehicle by the licence number, and then they were arrested by the public security and prosecuted before the District Court in Uzice in 1992. The perpetrators, I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any people killed as a result of these explosions?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nobody was killed. There were no casualties. There was only the physical destruction of the installations of the gas station and the damage at the tunnel at Chevron, some 20 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you did not further investigate the Severin kidnapping after your interview with Milan Lukic on the 26th and 27th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, as a member of the centre of the RDB Uzice, concerning that kidnapping, personally participated in the interview with Milan Lukic on the following day together with another two persons. That activity was in the exclusive jurisdiction of the third line of work that was in charge of everything that had to do with the extremism and terrorism, and the -- that kidnapping was treated as a terrorist act against the citizens of Serbia. Our orders were to get the service involved, and we did, in collecting information, but I did not have any tasks regarding that myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you further investigate Milan Lukic after your interview?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean I myself?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just asking about you.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, because after the interview that I conducted with a colleague, he was turned over to the public security in Uzice, because at the moment he was arrested, there was a suspicion that he was guilty of illegally carrying weapons and having false IDs, and there was a suspicion that he was involved in the murder of Stanko Pecikoza and the kidnapping of citizens of Serbia in the north. So he was investigated by the SUP, by the public security, and after that interview with us, he was turned over to them for further procession.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 6540. Since this is a longer document, I'm going to ask him to read a little bit of it. I was wondering if I could please have the Court Usher's assistance to provide the witness with the B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you jumped from the attack to the kidnapping. Is that the kidnapping we find on page 13974 and -77? I mean, you moved from --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I did move, and I changed -- I'm not talking about the -- I changed from the explosions in Kremna to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Sjeverin kidnapping.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- Sjeverin kidnapping. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it came a bit as, of course, a sudden change of subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar has difficulties in finding the relevant document in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could have the document taken back from the witness. I will check out what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could -- Mr. Novakovic, would you please be so kind to return the document to the usher. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any actions that were taken after Milan Lukic's arrest to further investigate the Sjeverin kidnappings?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the arrest of Milan Lukic and after interviewing him, my colleague and I conducted another interview with two other sources concerning the same circumstances, and both documents were turned over to the competent administration for further action. I don't know what happened later. I don't believe there was any interaction. I believe there was interaction between the centre and that authority, but I'm not familiar with the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated that one of the reasons that you were concerned -- or one of the reasons that you were concerned -- one the reasons you interviewed Milan Lukic was that you were concerned with the fate of the Muslim victims who were kidnapped. Is that correct? Is that one of the reasons that you went to interview Milan Lukic, to determine if he had any information about the kidnapped Muslims?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was precisely the reason. Those were the orders of the leadership of the service and even the state leadership at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could you always give us the pages and the lines so that we are better able to follow exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you not contact Risto Perisic, the chief of the Visegrad SUP, to ascertain any information that he may have had regarding this abduction?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no direct contact with Risto Perisic. I knew him because he came to Uzice sometimes, but not to talk to him. You see, it was happening at the moment when -- the kidnapping was on the 22nd, and I'm not sure now when the interview took place. At that time we didn't know the fate of the kidnapped people. It was within a very brief period of time the service was working on it, and I believe the operatives who were covering that territory, who were involved, were trying to get that information from the authorities in that territory. Risto Perisic was an official in the territory of Republika Srpska. You could not contact him as you wished, only as required. But this was a good reason to make an inquiry, but I was not directly involved. It was not directly my task.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, this witness, at transcript page 14140, previously testified that he did not know what happened to Milan Lukic after he took his statement and he was transferred to the Detention Unit. The Prosecution does have court records related to the charges that were sought after the interview and his release from custody on 4 November 1992. At this time, we would ask to tender these materials, which are available under 65 ter 6541.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: These -- these are -- this is a lengthy document. If the point is that the court released Milan Lukic, then perhaps we could deal with it shortly by just an agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we asked for the actual court records. It's three documents. It's the filing by the public prosecutor and the information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What -- what in addition to what Mr. Jordash seems to be willing to agree upon would you bring to our attention?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it the charges brought, or what is it? And how many pages are the documents altogether?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The B/C/S version is nine pages. The English translation is ten pages. The Prosecution would submit these are not voluminous records. They detail what was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- apologies to interrupt you, but the three documents all together is nine pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The problem we have is that within these documents there are a number of other names, including persons who were arrested with Lukic, and, on past practice, we have no faith that the Prosecution will not identify those people as perpetrators at some point and suggest the accused are responsible for them. So out of an abundance of caution, we have to object to any document which introduces new names which we have seen the Prosecution continuously trying to connect to the accused without notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, now we have two questions. My question: What is it that you want to establish beyond the fact that Mr. Lukic was released by the court? And second, whether you're going to rely on any of the other names mentioned in those documents so as to link them to the accused. Two questions. Could you please respond to both.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, with respect to the information in the documents, there's been other materials including the witness's statement, the statement of the Uzice public security --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, I put two simple questions to you. Now, you start with the second one, that's okay. I'm not asking to you in what context you want to use that in relation to what other evidence; the question was whether you are going to rely, perhaps together with other material, on the other names mentioned in that file.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I was trying to answer the first question. But to answer the second question is very simple: No. With respect to the first question, there's been -- the information, the details that are in the records here, when compared with other materials that have been introduced in the record, can show the information that was available to the authorities in October/November 1992 compared to later charges that were sought in relation to this offence that have already been made part of the record. So we would ask that -- we're not tendering a big volume of those court records; we're just asking that the materials be tendered. The individual that -- that is arrested with Milan Lukic on this has already been discussed, and information has already been admitted in relation to this individual. So in order to have -- for the Chamber to be able to see what he was addressed for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But purely Lukic, no one else?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: But he was arrested with someone else, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question simply was: Are you going to rely on these documents as well in relation to that other person? Now, you said the answer is very simple, "No." And then you started explaining how you will link those names to other evidence in relation to that person, which undermines your own answer, if I am --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If I've misunderstood Mr. Jordash's submission, I mean, the Defence is putting forward that they took certain actions against individuals, so there are two individuals that were arrested, and their release would be relevant to rebut the Defence contention. I guess to that extent I did contradict myself, and we would be relying upon the other individual to rebut that aspect of the Defence cases, to that extent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the questions to the witness were exclusively focusing on Mr. Lukic, isn't it, and not on the others?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at least during the course of his testimony he has testified as to the arrest of two individuals that were caught with what -- I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but have they been named? I mean, if Mr. Jordash has some fear that you'll link a specific individual to the accused, then if they slip in in what appears, at first, it seems to be about Lukic, then I would suggest that you put questions about that witness. I've got no idea who that other person is. I do -- I've got no idea whether he appears anywhere else in the evidence at this moment. So if you say you will use the name of that second person to rely upon in a broader context, then please lay a basis, lay a foundation for the use of that. Until now, when you tendered the document, we were not aware of anything else than that it was about Mr. Lukic. And that apparently is the fear of Mr. Jordash. So if you lay a foundation, we may reconsider that. Mr. Jordash, may I can take it that on the basis of the answers of Mr. Weber that you're not yet satisfied?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm not going to rely on this document for anything greater, or the identity of the second individual, anything greater than what I've already just explained on the record, which is that, at most, based on just the face of the document, that the individual was arrested with Milan Lukic, that they were detained, that they were processed on specific charges, and that Milan Lukic and this other individual were released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that other person, you're not going to link that other person in any way to what is the main subject of this trial, that is, that the accused may have some responsibility for what those persons did or --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Other than the arrest, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, without the Chamber even knowing who that other person is, not knowing, I mean it's -- it's -- if Mr. Jordash would not have objected, it would have slipped in. Now, the Chamber doesn't say that that is inadmissible evidence, but until now arrests and release of Mr. Lukic, there seems to be no problem. If you want this document to be in, and having received it also recently, then please tell us or identify with the witness who it was, how this linked to other evidence, so that we consider that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And the Prosecution doesn't intend to rely on this other individual in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What, then? If you're not interested in -- I take it that Mr. Jordash is willing to agree as well that not only Mr. Lukic was arrested and was later released by the court, but that there was another person which was arrested and released by the court. Well, if you don't want to rely on it in any further way, why do we need the document? If, however, you want to link that to other evidence, then at least the Chamber should know what person we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. Can we offer this -- these documents for the limited purpose of the fact that Milan Lukic was processed on certain charges based on the information in these documents and that he was then released on the 4th of November, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you -- can you agree on the charges which are laid out in the -- then we don't need the whole of the document. If you agree on the text of the charges as you find them in the document and if you agree on Milan Lukic being arrested and Milan Lukic being released by a court decision, then that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That would be fine, Your Honour, but could we also have an indication whether the Simatovic Defence would be willing to engage in such an agreement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll ask Mr. Petrovic and/or Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we are prepared to accept that kind of agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the only thing we still need is the text of the charges to be put on the record so that we know what the agreement is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we do that after a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I think that's appropriate. So you can use the break to copy it and perhaps OCR it. We'll take a break. And how much time would you still need after the break, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I was just going to go through one more document and that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One more document. We then resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit D784, marked for identification. Your Honours, I see the original version of this document appears to be not so great quality. I do have a hard copy available for the witness if it would assist him. If the Court Usher could please hand it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could please not look through the document yet. I'm going to ask you some questions about it and go through it with you briefly. I'd like to direct your first -- first your attention to the heading of the document. This document purports to be an Uzice CRDB Official Note of a preliminary interview of a source. Is it correct that the Roman numeral II in the heading represents the 2nd Administration?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you assigned or performed any tasks on behalf of the 2nd Administration of the Uzice CRDB in April of 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to explain that to you yesterday, but you interrupted me. If I may say it now. In late 1994 and early 1995, the issues at the headquarters of the service that had intelligence connotations were slowly being transferred to another service. Everything was directed to the 3rd Administration that dealt with terrorism and extremism. That is the consequence of the situation in the service itself. Until 1991, this was dealt with by the federal service. And after that, republic services started developing intelligence activities in their own centres. And this is a direct consequence of this. The contact with this source is a contact with a source who provides intelligence, and that is why I directed it to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You said a couple of things here. If I could go back to my question. Were you assigned or did you perform any tasks for the 2nd Administration of the Uzice CRDB in April 1995? If your answer is "yes," could you please tell us what that task was?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Already from the end of 1994, and in this period to which your question relates, I was oriented mostly, although as a member of the centre, I was in charge of intelligence. I also dealt with intelligence work, collecting all information, all intelligence of interest to the republic regarding economy, politics, defence, and security, anything relevant to the security of the country, the national security. And since intelligence work implies also collecting all information about any threats to national and cultural and economic integrity of the Serbs, wherever they live, I also collected information on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, page 35, line 21/22, the witness makes a distinction between types of information in terms of different lines of work, but I believe this distinction is not clear in the transcript, at least not quite as the witness put it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll try to clarify that. Mr. Weber, perhaps -- I think sometimes the line numbering is not exactly the same. Mr. Petrovic, would you be willing to read in English the line you had on your mind, and then we'll ask the witness whether what you read to him is his complete answer or whether further details were mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can, Your Honour. "... I was oriented mostly, although as a member of the centre, I was in charge of intelligence. I also dealt with intelligence work, collecting all information, all intelligence of interest to the republic regarding economy," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you make any further -- did you mention any further detail as far as intelligence was concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said: Although I was dealing with counter-intelligence work, in that period I started also collecting intelligence information, because that was the demand of the service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever conduct any interviews of this source Producent?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sources are within the scope of the -- I don't know whether the answer to your question would possibly identify --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm not asking for the identity of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, so you're clear: I'm not asking for the identity of the source in my question. I just would like to know whether or not you ever conducted any interviews of this source.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please move to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us the name of the source?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Coming here, I got a decision from the Government of Serbia waiving my obligation to keep official secrets. Sources are the highest asset of the service, and they are protected, and when I got retired, I signed the Official Secrets Act requiring me to keep secrets on all sources, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the Republic of Serbia has requested protective measures. We have decided on that, and we do protect sources. That's the reason why we are in private session and why we're not dealing with this matter in public. The Republic of Serbia is informed about the decision the Chamber, and if they would have wished to -- to appeal that or to have that reviewed, they would have had an opportunity to do that. So therefore, we're in private session. It will not be public. And you're invited to answer the question. Apparently there's no problem as far as the Republic of Serbia is concerned. Would you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know whether this source is still being used today. That's why I'm saying what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's the reason why we are in private session. That's the reason why we would not make this publicly known. Everyone in this courtroom is under an obligation to keep it secret, and this part of your testimony will not be broadcasted to the outside world. Please answer the question, Mr. Novakovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you would clarify it, Mr. Weber. That's okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, the interpreter believes that they might have heard something additional after you said the name of the source. They

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please review that document. Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to read it aloud?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. No. If you could review the document and let us know if you authored it.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Review it until you're able to determine whether or not you're familiar with it and whether or not you authored it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, I think the question of Mr. Weber was that when you're able to say that you recognise this document or that you authored it, that please let us know. And then whether you have to read, then, the whole of it or whether certain portions will be put to you by Mr. Weber, we'll see that. But do you recognise the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do recognise the document, and, yes, I authored it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then listen carefully to the questions Mr. Weber will put to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last paragraph of this Official Note contains a recommendation. It states: "We believe it is necessary for the leadership of the centre in the 2nd Administration of the RDB MUP RS to urgently agree on how precisely the source should be used and to examine (redacted). On the front of the Official Note, it indicated that this was just a preliminary interview. Did you conduct any subsequent interviews or generate any subsequent reports in addition to this source?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, you can see from the content of this document that there is a wide array of information provided. The situation in the political segments of Republika Srpska, the situation in the army, the situation on the ground. My thinking in terms of this contact and also in agreement with the 2nd Administration, the further guidelines to be provided to this source were to be co-ordinated. I did continue my relationship with this contact or source.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you generate any later reports in relation to those subsequent contacts?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I must have written reports, because I wrote things up whenever I had contact with him. Perhaps until 1995, 1996. It had to do with the subject matter of Bosnia, later on perhaps something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we -- I believe we're still in private session. If we could return to open session. I have a number of housekeeping matters to hopefully alleviate from next week, and I also wanted to read in an agreed fact. I'm done --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does this mean that your cross-examination of the witness is concluded?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions. Then we return into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Now, before we deal with practical matters, Mr. Weber, are they of such urgency that we should first hear them before we give an opportunity to the Defence to put further questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I think so, because the Prosecution's going to be withdrawing a number of objections that we have had, and if this is of assistance to the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that -- if that -- if that -- if that is relevant information in relation to the further examination of this witness, then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time withdraws its objection to the admission of the comment chart of the witness marked for identification as D424. However, the Prosecution maintains its submissions regarding the probative value and weight of these comments. The Prosecution also withdraws its objection to the admission of the following exhibits: D427, D430, D432, D435, D437, D440, D443, and D784. Lastly, the Prosecution withdraws its objection to exhibit -- to the admission of Exhibit D436. However, the quality of this document is poor. We would inquire whether or not the Defence has a better available version, and if not, the Prosecution requests verification of the translation of the last paragraph on page 1 of the B/C/S original after the words "Visegrada sevsto [phoen]," as this may contain relevant information. With that, Your Honour, I'd seek leave to read in an agreed fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And if the Defence has a better version available, is then the request for the verification of the translation moot? Or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct. If we're able to see it and it corresponds to what is available on the translation, then that would render the need to do a verification moot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then there's a fair chance that these exhibits would be admitted into evidence. I would have to look at it. The Chamber will have to look at it, of course, in further detail what the basis of the objections were, whether we have any questions in relation to those. But I think there would be a fair expectation that admission is forthcoming. Any other matter, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could please read in the agreed fact related to the matter that was addressed just before the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The following information would be agreed upon between the parties: On 30 October 1992, Milan Lukic was charged with the crime of unauthorised procurement, possession, carrying, manufacture, exchange or sale of weapons, ammunition, and explosive substances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please slow down, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On 4 November 1992, the District Court in Uzice dismissed these charges as unfounded and terminated the detention of Milan Lukic. He was then released from custody. So stipulated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then that is on the record that the parties agree on these facts. Who will go first?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that it should be the Defence of Mr. Simatovic. That is the way we usually handle things. Of course, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine with me. Could you give us a time estimate, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, only a few minutes. Not more than ten at any rate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, could you give us an indication already?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Not more than 15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then please proceed, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Further Cross-examination by Mr. Petrovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Novakovic.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at P3169, and could the document please not be displayed to the public. P3169 is the document number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, a few moments ago you looked at this document. I would just like to put a few questions to you in relation to the document. I would like to start with the first sentence. It says there: "In the period between the 18th of June and the 25th of June, 1995, I went to Srebrenica on a number of occasions with the knowledge of the Service." Mr. Novakovic, will you agree with me that Srebrenica was taken by the Army of Republika Srpska on the 11th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but that was probably the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that before Srebrenica was taken by the Army of Republika Srpska, it had not been possible for anyone to go to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Novakovic. Next sentence. "In the aforementioned period, I met Milan Lukic at the hotel in Bratunac." Mr. Novakovic, what is your understanding of this sentence, "I met Milan Lukic"?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That absolutely means that he saw him in passing. It means that he saw him, saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When we analyse the meaning of this sentence, does this sentence in any way suggest that they had agreed to meet, that they had had any meeting as such whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. I think that that's absolutely not suggested, because in view of the document that he's writing, I think that he would have mentioned in the document had he been on that kind of mission, that he met with him, that he told him something. Because he says here, "I met Milan Lukic," and he describes what happened. He describes that he saw him wearing a uniform. He's saying what he saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had there been a meeting apart from this encounter, would it be expected to have this noted in the Official Note, not only to refer to the appearance, the physical appearance of the person?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. He would have said what the subject discussed with the said person was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the second paragraph of the same document. The same document. It says: "The same group equipped in the same manner, I encountered 10 or 15 days later."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphones for the Judges, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, this is a document which, of course, when interpreted, then will be commented by the parties. Now, whether the witness is a person who is the one who should guide us in interpreting this document is very questionable. We'd rather hear facts from this witness. There seems to be, however, one thing that is -- reference was made to -- I -- let me see. I think you're -- or consistently the word is -- the word is used -- let me check that, because it just disappeared from my screen. Yes. What you read was, as it appears on the transcript, "In the aforementioned period, I met Milan Lukic at the hotel in Bratunac"; whereas the translation says "I met up with." That may not be exactly the same. That's one. And then in the answer, the witness says -- gives his interpretation of what that means, to see in passing. The Chamber is not fully aware of what makes this witness a person that could tell us exactly that meeting up with a certain person would actually mean see him in passing. Again, that interpretation, you could call 50 other witnesses who would tell us what the meaning of this document is. We rather hear facts. And we'd rather have the right quote, "meet up with" rather than "met." And if there's any translation issue in that respect, we'd like to know so that can be verified. Please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- if you allow me. If you allow me. If you allow me just one sentence. My intention is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As long as what you say is something that could be appropriately said without the witness taking off his earphones or, if he speaks English, to leave the courtroom. Then you have an opportunity. But no further discussion about the content of evidence in the presence of a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
